import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load data from attached files
unknown = files[0] if files[0]['filename'] == 'T120.csv' else files[1]
library = files[1] if files[0]['filename'] == 'T120.csv' else files[0]

x_unk = unknown['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
y_unk = unknown['table']['intensity']

# Normalize unknown spectrum (min-max)
y_unk_norm = (y_unk - np.min(y_unk)) / (np.max(y_unk) - np.min(y_unk))

ref_ids = library['table']['spectrum_id']
ref_mats = library['table']['material']
ref_x = library['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
ref_y = library['table']['intensity']

unique_ids = np.unique(ref_ids)
best_corr = -1
best_id = None
best_mat = None
best_y = None

for sid in unique_ids:
    mask = (ref_ids == sid)
    # Check if this spectrum has the same length as unknown (should be 1801)
    curr_x = ref_x[mask]
    curr_y = ref_y[mask]
    
    if len(curr_y) != len(y_unk):
        continue
        
    # Normalize reference spectrum
    y_ref_norm = (curr_y - np.min(curr_y)) / (np.max(curr_y) - np.min(curr_y))
    
    # Calculate Pearson Correlation Coefficient
    corr = np.corrcoef(y_unk_norm, y_ref_norm)[0, 1]
    
    if corr > best_corr:
        best_corr = corr
        best_id = sid
        # Get material for this id (first occurrence)
        best_mat = ref_mats[mask][0]
        best_y = curr_y

print(f"Best Match ID: {best_id}")
print(f"Material: {best_mat}")
print(f"Correlation: {best_corr:.4f}")

# Plotting for verification
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(x_unk, y_unk / np.max(y_unk), label='Unknown (T120)', color='black', linewidth=2)
plt.plot(ref_x[ref_ids == best_id], best_y / np.max(best_y), label=f'Best Match: {best_mat} ({best_id})', color='red', linestyle='--')
plt.title(f"Comparison of Unknown Spectrum T120 and Best Library Match")
plt.xlabel("Raman Shift (cm-1)")
plt.ylabel("Normalized Intensity")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.savefig('best_match_comparison.png')
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Find files
unknown = None
library = None
for f in files:
    if f['filename'] == 'T120.csv':
        unknown = f
    elif f['filename'] == 'reference_library.csv':
        library = f

x_unk = unknown['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
y_unk = unknown['table']['intensity']

# Library columns
ref_ids = library['table']['spectrum_id']
ref_mats = library['table']['material']
ref_x = library['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
ref_y = library['table']['intensity']

# Group data by spectrum_id manually to avoid masking issues
spectra_dict = {}
unique_ids = np.unique(ref_ids)

for sid in unique_ids:
    # Use list comprehension for indexing if numpy masks are acting weird
    indices = [i for i, val in enumerate(ref_ids) if val == sid]
    if len(indices) > 0:
        spectra_dict[sid] = {
            'x': ref_x[indices],
            'y': ref_y[indices],
            'mat': ref_mats[indices][0]
        }

print(f"Loaded {len(spectra_dict)} spectra from library.")
for sid, data in spectra_dict.items():
    print(f"{sid}: {data['mat']}, length={len(data['x'])}")

# Now find the best match using Pearson Correlation on normalized intensities
best_corr = -1
best_id = None
best_mat = None

for sid, data in spectra_dict.items():
    y_ref = data['y']
    if len(y_ref) != len(y_unk):
        continue
    
    # Correlation coefficient (Pearson) is invariant to scale and offset
    corr = np.corrcoef(y_unk, y_ref)[0, 1]
    if corr > best_corr:
        best_corr = corr
        best_id = sid
        best_mat = data['mat']

print(f"\nBest Match ID: {best_id}")
print(f"Material: {best_mat}")
print(f"Correlation: {best_corr:.4f}")

if best_id:
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    plt.plot(x_unk, y_unk / np.max(y_unk), label='Unknown (T120)', color='black', lw=2)
    plt.plot(spectra_dict[best_id]['x'], spectra_dict[best_id]['y'] / np.max(spectra_dict[best_id]['y']), 
             label=f'Best Match: {best_mat} ({best_id})', color='red', ls='--')
    plt.title(f"Comparison of T120 and Best Library Match")
    plt.xlabel("Raman Shift (cm-1)")
    plt.ylabel("Normalized Intensity")
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.savefig('best_match_T120.png')
